key_insight: A 3D global stability analysis shows that screech in turbulent under-expanded jets can be explained by coupled Kelvin–Helmholtz and shock-cell feedback modes, even at high under-expansion levels.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and interpret jet-noise resonance mechanisms, supporting nozzle design strategies aimed at reducing screech and improving aeroacoustic performance.
method: URANS fixed-point solutions computed with the dNami compressible-flow solver
Linearised discrete system obtained via automatic differentiation with Tapenade
3D time-stepping global stability analysis plus Helmholtz decomposition and energy budgeting
evidence_signal: The extracted modes were validated against experimental data and POD results, reproducing the main wavenumber content and spatial organisation of the screech resonance loop.
watch_item: The analysis relies on URANS fixed points and linearised modes, so nonlinear transient effects and sensitivity to modelling choices may limit direct transfer to different nozzle conditions.
paper_title: Three-dimensional global stability analysis of turbulent screeching jets
